title: Jamaican Fried Dumplings
subtitle: Crisp golden dumplings fried in oil
excerpt: Small rounds of plain flour dough, fried until the outside is crisp and the inside is soft and doughy. A Jamaican breakfast staple served with ackee and saltfish or callaloo.
sourceNotes: Classic Jamaican johnnycake / festival variant; fried dumplings are a breakfast staple across Jamaica.

recipe.batchNotes: Double the dough and fry in batches. Keep cooked dumplings warm in a low oven.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix and shape the dumplings up to an hour ahead. Keep covered at room temperature.

content.text: Jamaican fried dumplings are small, dense rounds of flour dough cooked in hot oil. They give a crisp shell with a soft, chewy centre. Keep the oil at a steady medium heat so they cook through before the outside darkens.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in the bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the water a little at a time. Bring the dough together with your hands until smooth and not sticky.
Rest the dough for 5 minutes under a clean cloth.
Divide into 8 equal pieces. Roll each into a ball and flatten slightly to about 1.5cm thick.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. The oil is ready when a small piece of dough sizzles immediately.
Fry the dumplings in batches for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Lift out with the slotted spoon and drain on a piece of kitchen paper. Serve warm.

items.symptom: The outsides are dark but the centres are raw.
items.fix: Lower the heat to medium-low. Fry slowly so the heat reaches the centre before the crust darkens.

items.cause: The oil was not hot enough when they went in.
items.fix: Always test the oil temperature with a small scrap of dough first.
Add water one teaspoon at a time until the dough is smooth and pliable.
